children: Australian equities rose 33 points, or 0.4%, to 8,838 in early Monday trade, extending prior gains and marking their highest level in more than five weeks.
Sentiment was buoyed by a rebound in U.S. equity futures after last week’s chip-sector rout, with investors shifting focus to earnings amid mounting pressure on the AI sector.
Locally, softer-than-expected labor data cooled bets on a near-term rate hike by the Reserve Bank.
However, caution ahead of key releases in top trading partner China later today, including September activity, home prices, and Q3 GDP, tempered gains.
Energy minerals and industrial services led the rise, with Nextdc Ltd. (3.6%), AGL Energy (1.7%), and Whitehaven Coal (1.2%) among notable movers.
Challenger Ltd. surged 14.5% after TAL Dai-ichi Life reportedly made a non-binding takeover proposal at AUD 11.80 per share.
Meanwhile,  the four big banks added between 0.9% and 1.3%.
In contrast,  BHP Group slipped 0.5%, and Rio Tinto edged down 0.2%.

title: Australian Shares Hover at Over 5-Week High as Week Opens
